title: Peninsula VineHop Festival 2026
summary: A one-day craft drinks festival across seven Mornington Peninsula venues on Saturday 21 November 2026, with tastings, food and live music. The event runs from 11am to 7pm and is strictly 18+, with shuttle, general admission and private bus options.
venueName: Festival Hub at The Briars and six linked venues
priceRange: Paid, with Festival Hub, general admission, shuttle and private bus options
suitableFor: Adults aged 18 and over; wine, beer, cider and spirits drinkers; groups
accessibilityNotes: Check accessibility arrangements with the organiser before booking. The festival spans seven separate venues and uses shuttle transport.
weatherDependency: Moderate, with outdoor movement between venues. Check the organiser's updates before travelling.
verificationStatus: Verified against official VineHop website and Humanitix ticket page on 2026-08-25
nearbyAttractions: The Briars, Mount Martha village, Balnarring and Red Hill wine country
suggestedItineraryPairing: Choose one shuttle loop for the day, or stay at the Festival Hub at The Briars if you want a simpler base with parking.
editorVerdict: The shuttle ticket is the cleanest way to make a day of VineHop. The Festival Hub works better if you want one venue, parking and the main stage.
editorNote:
VineHop is a one-day, adults-only craft drinks festival spread across seven venues on the Mornington Peninsula. The 2026 edition runs on Saturday 21 November from 11am to 7pm, with tastings, food trucks, bars and live music. The Festival Hub at The Briars is the largest base and includes free on-site parking, while the other venues are designed to be reached by the festival buses or private transport.

The seven venues are Festival Hub at The Briars in Mount Martha, Devilbend Farm Beer, Phaedrus Estate, Stumpy Gully, Hickinbotham of Dromana, Mock Red Hill, and The Pig and Whistle Tavern featuring Tallarida. North and South shuttle tickets cover four venues on their route, transport and tastings. The published pickup times are around 10.30am to 11.15am, depending on the stop. Buses begin circulating between venues from 11.30am.

General admission covers all seven venues but not transport. It suits a group with a private VineHop bus or a clear plan for taxis between stops. Drivers cannot attend as patrons, there is no parking at the smaller venues, and groups of 12 or more must use a VineHop private or shuttle bus. The event is strictly 18+, with no refunds listed on the ticket page.

Ticket tiers and availability can change, so check Humanitix before booking. The practical choice for a first visit is a shuttle ticket, unless the Festival Hub's music and parking are the main draw.
